## Step 1 · The total of each group: a PivotTable {.study}

{{< watch title="Create a PivotTable" source="Microsoft Support" url="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/create-a-pivottable-to-analyze-worksheet-data" length="0:45" checked="2026-10-31" captions="English" >}}

- A long list has many rows. You want **one total for each group** (each
  type, each department).
- A **PivotTable** does it in a few clicks: **Insert › PivotTable**.
- Put the group in **Rows** and the number in **Values** (Sum).
- Check: the **Grand Total** is the total of the whole list.

::: {.callout-note title="Model · Rana's month"}
Rana has 24 sales of March in a list. She wants the total of each type.
She makes a PivotTable: Rows **Type**, Values **Sum of Total**. Paper 206
JD, Drinks 71 JD, Bags 78 JD; Grand Total 355 JD.
:::

**On a computer or on the web.** The orange numbers show where to click.

::: {.screens}
![[1]{.step-n} Click in the list, then **Insert**. [2]{.step-n} Click **PivotTable**. [3]{.step-n} Click **OK**.](images/pivot-win-1.png)

![In **PivotTable Fields**: [4]{.step-n} tick the group (Type): it goes to **Rows**. [5]{.step-n} Tick the number (Total): it goes to **Values**. [6]{.step-n} Read the totals and the **Grand Total**.](images/pivot-win-2.png)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/pivot-lab.html" poster="sims/pivot-lab.png" title="Pivot Lab: summarize Rana's month" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · PivotTables"}
Use Rana's month. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Values: Type|355 rows"}
Where does the group (Type) go?
:   Rows

    Why: Rows give one line for each type.

Where does the number (Total) go?
:   Values

    Why: Values add the numbers of each group.

What is the Grand Total of Rana's month?
:   355 JD

    Why: 206 + 71 + 78 = 355: the total of the whole list.
:::
:::

## Step 2 · What the data shows, and a chart {.study}

{{< watch title="Create charts" source="Microsoft Support" url="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/create-a-chart-from-start-to-finish" length="0:52" checked="2026-10-31" captions="English" >}}

- Read the PivotTable: **which group is the biggest**? Which is the
  smallest? Is one group **half** of the total?
- A true sentence about the data, with a number, helps a manager decide.
- A **column chart** compares the groups: click the PivotTable, then
  **Insert › Column chart**.

::: {.callout-note title="Model · What Rana's month shows"}
Paper 206 of 355 JD: more than half of the money. So Rana orders more
paper for April. The column of Paper in the chart is the tallest.
:::

**On a computer or on the web.** The orange numbers show where to click.

::: {.screens}
![Click in the PivotTable. [1]{.step-n} Click **Insert**. [2]{.step-n} Click the **Column chart** button and the first chart.](images/pivot-chart-1.png)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/chart-lab.html" poster="sims/chart-lab.png" title="Chart Lab: the right chart for the question" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · What the data shows"}
Rana's month: Paper 206, Drinks 71, Bags 78 JD (355 in all). Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="Drinks|a pie of every sale"}
Which type brought the most money?
:   Paper

    Why: 206 is the biggest total.

Is Paper more than half of the money: yes or no?
:   yes

    Why: Half of 355 is about 178, and 206 is more.

Which chart compares the three types?
:   a column chart

    Why: Columns side by side compare amounts.
:::
:::

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

Open the start file `training.xlsx`: the training hours of the Sunrise
staff (12 rows). (Step 1 shows how.)

### Task 1 · A PivotTable

1. Make a PivotTable: Rows **Department**, Values **Sum of Hours**.
2. Click the PivotTable and insert a **column chart**.
3. Save the file as `training.xlsx`.

*Submit:* the file `training.xlsx`.

### Task 2 · What the data shows

a) Which department has the most hours? **A** Sales · **B** Office · **C**
Shop. Write the letter.

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) Make a second PivotTable with Rows **Course**. Which sentence is true?
**A** Safety has more hours than Word. · **B** Half of all the hours are
Excel. · **C** Word has the most hours. Write the letter. (Step 2 shows
how.)

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}
